<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9ad898e05498d800d9a9153254c22d8d130e23ce` — the merge of head `8be0f346f3eee9fe8bd6642b97fe1f8cff729a81` into base `ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9ad898e05498d800d9a9153254c22d8d130e23ce && git checkout 9ad898e05498d800d9a9153254c22d8d130e23ce
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394 8be0f346f3eee9fe8bd6642b97fe1f8cff729a81 && git checkout -B drift-repro ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394 && git merge --no-ff 8be0f346f3eee9fe8bd6642b97fe1f8cff729a81

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8be0f346f3eee9fe8bd6642b97fe1f8cff729a81`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `.changeset/32335-compose-nested-artifact-action-bodies.md`, `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/compose-stacks-action-key-collision.test.ts` + `packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts`, `packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts`, `packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts` (cited code, read on `main`, not reviewed)

Inputs read: card #32335 body and all 6 comments; PR #32475 body, its file list (3 files, +250/-14) and the net diff against `main`; the check-runs on this head (every run `success` or `skipped`; none failed or pending).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `composeStacks`: narrowed only. Right.** Step 6 now also notes the action keys each `packages[K]` body of an input declares. A nested input's key reachable only through its top level still refuses (`topLevel` returns false in `composedPackagesHoldApart`). Reading bodies only adds declarers, so no composition refused before is admitted now.
- **Flat inputs: unchanged. Right.** An input without `packages[]` adds nothing in the new walk, and its holder is still `manifest.id` / `manifest.namespace`.
- **New refusals, each right against the boot code on `main`:**
  - nested artifact plus a third package of one body's namespace, under either manifest (the install gate reads the same predicate: `bareNameHoldersMeet` calls `namespacedHoldersMeet`);
  - nested artifact plus a package of another namespace, under the default manifest: `actionBindingGroups` finds one holder for the key (the body) and binds the third package's top-level declaration under that body's package, so one body is silently shadowed. The refusal names `preserve`, and the pair composes under `preserve`;
  - an object-bound key a body's object embeds, against another input's declaration of the same `OBJECT:NAME` (one-holder rule kept);
  - two nested inputs carrying the same package id count as one holder, as the flat pair does.
- **Public surface: unchanged. Right.** Two private interfaces and one private helper; no export, schema key or shape changes; no `api-surface` file in the diff. `StackComposeActionKeyCollisionError` keeps its code and 422; its `issues` text gains `packages[K]…` sites.
- **Holder identity: right.** `composedBodyHolder` reads `id || name` and treats an empty namespace as none, the same spelling as `artifactPackageId` and the boot's holder read.
- **Gate verdicts:** Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core, Type Check, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness and Governed Surface Queue Guard are all `success` on this head.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec: minor` with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` matches: AGENTS.md puts a protocol kind at least `minor` on a package the diff moves.
- The breaking-change duties are met: the BREAKING banner, the FROM/TO fix, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`).
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, carries the same FROM admits / TO refused statement, and matches the diff (nothing widened). No `skip-changeset` label.
- The census of 0 is consistent: the one first-party caller composes flat inputs with no actions, and the full suite and dogfood gate are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- **Out-of-scope finding, escalated to a follow-up card:** `mergeObjects` walks top-level objects only. A stripped nested artifact whose body declares object `X`, composed beside an input that also declares `X`, passes under `objectConflict: 'error'` where the flat pair is refused. The new walk then skips the body's `X` actions on the premise that the object door already judged that object, so an `X:approve` embedded on both sides is admitted and the body's object is silently replaced at boot. This is the object door's gap, not this card's action rule. The seat files it; it does not block this head.
- Deviations accepted: the PR-body line order follows the seat's order file; the shallow fetch of the self-test's pinned commit touches nothing in the diff. The two local gates that exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) are answered by CI (`Lint & Repo Gates` `success`).
- Lane: within triage 6796273876. The spec hunk rides this PR because no key, schema shape or export moves.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away.

- On `main`, the `composeStacks` docblock already says that two input stacks whose declarations resolve to one scope-qualified action key throw. `packages` is a `concat` key, so a nested input is a legal input. Skipping package bodies was a gap in that refusal, not a capability.
- The one admitted pair is still delivered: a nested artifact beside a package of another namespace still composes under `preserve` (pinned by a CONTROL).
- Cases tried by reading, none broke it:
  - a nested input that keeps a flattened copy: same stack index, so no self-collision, and still refused through `topLevel`;
  - a `defineStack` echo inside a body: same stack, not counted;
  - a hybrid input: holders are read from the bodies;
  - a body with no id: refused (conservative);
  - three holders across two bodies and a flat input: judged pairwise;
  - a nested-plus-flat `preserve` output keeps its flattened copy (`packagesReproduceComposedCollections` fails on length), and two stripped nested inputs leave no composed objects to skip against.
- No must-fix or should-fix. Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract), left as accepted deviations:
  - the `stack.zod.ts` jsdoc says "so compose and install refuse the same pairs", but under the default manifest compose also refuses the two-namespace pair install admits, by design;
  - the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet holds for the verdict, not the text: a nested input that keeps a flattened copy now also lists its `packages[K].actions[J]` site in `issues`;
  - a body action record with no `name` keys as `global:undefined`, as a top-level one does; reachable only by a hand-built body;
  - a flat holder's id is `manifest.id`, a body's is `id || name` (the flat side predates this diff and errs toward refusal).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`composeStacks` 第 6 步（跨栈动作键冲突检查）现在也读「嵌套产物」（自带 `packages[]` 的输入，例如 preserve 组合出的多包产物）里每个包体的动作，并用安装门的同一条命名空间规则（`namespacedHoldersMeet`）判定。
- 为什么改：多包产物只在包体里带动作，旧检查只看顶层，所以「嵌套产物 + 与其中某包同命名空间、声明同名对象外动作的第三个包」会被放行；逐个安装同样三个包时，第三个会被拒（NAMESPACE_CONFLICT）。放行后启动的结果是：preserve 下两个地址都 409，谁都调不到；默认 manifest 下静默只跑第三个包的。
- 风险与回滚：只收窄（BREAKING）：上述组合原本放行，现在改为 422 STACK_COMPOSE_ACTION_KEY_COLLISION；不带 `packages[]` 的输入判法不变；第一方普查为 0。只改 spec 一个文件的私有函数，runtime 不动；回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` 第 6 步新增的包体遍历和 `composedPackagesHoldApart`；`compose-stacks-action-key-collision.test.ts` 末尾新增的 describe。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/compose-stacks-action-key-collision.test.ts`，预期 41/41 通过。
- 需要你做的：席位的落地动作被本会话的自动模式分类器拦下（同 #32464），需要你在线程里授权，或者你直接转 ready 合并。

席位意见：ACCEPT。收窄让 spec 自己声明的拒收真正生效，没有拿走任何已声明能力；契约档复核 PASS，只有 nit。复核发现的对象门同类缺口（嵌套包体里的对象不受 `objectConflict: 'error'` 约束）已立卡 #32477，不挡本 PR。

## 席位核对

1. Shape: draft PR to `main`; `Fixes #32335` is its only closing keyword, and it sits beside no other open card number. 3 files: `stack.zod.ts`, one test file and the changeset, all within the claim's surface as amended in 6807368544. The changeset is `@objectstack/spec` minor with a BREAKING banner, FROM/TO fix, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, a `Skills-docs:` line, and one ADR-0087 `not-required` marker. I checked its sentences against the diff and they match, except the nit the review names (the "Unchanged" bullet holds for the verdict, not the `issues` text).
2. Premise measured: step 0 (`/mnt/project-files/server-seat3-p2/32335/step0.md`, on `14754c70`) reproduced the four cases. The pins cover all four, plus an object-bound case, and assert `code`, `status` and the `issues` path. One ablation went 4 red / 37 green and was restored.
3. Gates on head `8be0f346`: every check-run is `success` or an expected skip (56 success, 11 skipped, 0 other), including Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core and the Dogfood Regression Gate. `mergeable_state` is `clean`; K = 4.
4. Accepted deviations: the 4 nits in the contract review stay as they are. The two local gates that exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) are answered by CI. Contract review: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER PASS, comment 6809232138, on this head (claim 6809163360).
5. Out of scope: the `mergeObjects` gap is filed as #32477 (p2, pm:queue). Skills-docs: none (`skills/**` names `composeStacks` only as an existence pointer).
6. Landing: not governed (`packages/spec/src/**` is a contract face, not a governed path), 264 lines ≤ 3000, Tier S on the contract-tier PASS. It is held with `pm:awaiting-merge`, behind the same auto-mode classifier refusal as #32464 (Merge Without Review). The landing stroke was not attempted again.
